cpu: Intel Core i5-12400 (6 cores, 12 logical CPUs)
method: Ten independent identical synthetic file copies; inputs are warm. Buffer inputs preloaded before timing. A batch retains all complete JS results until Promise.all resolves. One full-batch warmup and five measured batches, forced GC before each. Cases run serially in fresh Node processes. Main thread user+system CPU from process.threadCpuUsage, event loop activity from eventLoopUtilization. A 1ms heartbeat and serial fs.stat every 10ms run during each batch. Filesystem probe timings include scheduling and JS callback delivery; not a pure libuv queue measure.
measurementNotes: Main-thread CPU includes JavaScript, Node-API value construction, synchronous input snapshots, main-thread GC, and probe overhead; it is not JS-only instruction time or one continuous stall.
Event-loop utilization measures time outside the loop event provider, not CPU consumption. It can rise as the same main-thread work is delivered in less wall time.
Heartbeat values are observed callback gaps (not strict deadlines). Tables use medians of per-batch maxima; see all samples for outliers.

Process peak RSS covers warmup and all five batches. Complete output is retained until all requests finish. Different GC/allocator states prevent treating this as an isolated per-operation memory bound.

Original explicit-limit cases use commit 6d6ee6f. cpu-default-change cases use the following uncommitted default-only implementation identified by source and native hashes. Build/check processes did not overlap measurements.
The same metric code ran in both sets. The archived helper adds default-limit selection, formatting, and an equivalent RSS unit expression after the original cases.
No production files or services were accessed. Results describe these local synthetic workloads on Node 22 only, not every file, runtime or CPU.
After measurement, the archived helper replaces its captured boolean stop flag with AbortController for lint compliance; the sampling schedule and metric calculations are unchanged.
